title: Deep Learning for RF Device Fingerprinting in Cognitive Communication Networks

dataset.data_volume: 7,000 transmissions total (1,000 valid transmissions per device across 7 devices), split into 17 non-overlapping segments of 1,024 samples per transmission
dataset.participants_devices: 7 Digi XBP24CZ7SITB003 ZigBee Pro devices operating in the 2.4 GHz band
dataset.experimental_conditions: Transmissions on IEEE 802.15.4 channel 11 (2.405 GHz center frequency) configured at maximum power level of 18 dBm with 16 MHz sampling rate. Outdoor experiment used Pulse Electronics W1030 omni-directional antennas at approximately 30 meters distance in an urban outdoor environment with an estimated in-band SNR of ~28 dB. Lab experiment used direct hardwired connections through a power splitter with simulated AWGN added in the range -10, 15, 20,..., 40 dB.
dataset.data_split: 80% training data, 10% validation data, and 10% testing data

accuracy.method_model: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) operating on time-domain complex baseband error signal
accuracy.experimental_condition: Outdoor urban environment at ~28 dB SNR using 7 Digi ZigBee devices
accuracy.evaluation_setting: Closed-set identification on test set (10% test data)

limitation: For both experiments overfitting was observed during the late stages of training.

evidence.text: We develop a framework for training a convolutional neural network using the time-domain complex baseband error signal and demonstrate 92.29% identification accuracy on a set of 7 2.4 GHz commercial ZigBee devices.
